source.title: Predicting the Generalization Gap in Deep Networks with Margin Distributions
source.authors: Yiding Jiang; Dilip Krishnan; H. Mobahi; Samy Bengio

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a result for a network trained with 20% corrupted labels, measuring training and test accuracy; it does not test the full random-labeling claim or a corruption sweep.
record.gate_note: The text cites Zhang et al. for fitting randomly labeled data, but that cited result is not this study’s result. Figure 1 reports one network trained with 20% corrupted labels; the other networks’ label conditions are not stated.
record.test_reason: The study trains CIFAR-10 networks using SGD with momentum and measures training and test accuracy, including a 20% label-corruption condition. These are the original experimental method and measures for the tested part of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: normalized margin distributions across multiple layers strongly predict generalization gap. The authors emphasize normalization, hidden-layer information, and distribution summaries combined in log space; they do not establish the full random-label or corruption-sweep claims.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains CIFAR-10 networks with 20% corrupted labels and reports training and test accuracy, rather than testing completely random labels or sweeping corruption levels.
record.method_sensitivity: The text describes networks and settings with varying test accuracy, but does not report a label-corruption sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized margin distributions across multiple layers predict generalization gaps across architectures and hyperparameter settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layerwise normalized margin statistics predict generalization gap.

record.problems: For the claim-relevant result, only one 20% corruption condition is described; no chance-level comparison, uncertainty estimate, or corruption sweep is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results are reported. Figure 1 gives test accuracies for two additional networks, but their label conditions are not stated and therefore they do not establish results on the listed versions.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, chance test accuracy, and fitting without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true and random labels, and convergence slowing with increasing corruption.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect fitting throughout a corruption sweep and steadily rising test error toward chance. One 20% corruption example cannot establish these trends.

Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent fitting completely random labels; generalization after removing weight decay, dropout, or all regularizers together; matched effects of removing augmentation.
The order in which shared real-data patterns and noisy labels are learned.

missing.what: A ResNet-32 trained on CIFAR-10 achieves 91.7% test accuracy without data augmentation, providing evidence for the augmentation component of V5.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 limits_scope verdict confuses incomplete coverage with an observed limitation. No corruption-dependent failure is established. Section 4.1 reports deliberately lowered training accuracy under strong weight regularization, but does not identify the label conditions of those models, so that statement cannot establish a V4 or random-label V5 challenge.

versions.untested_parts: Complete random labeling and chance test error.
Training time and convergence rate across corruption levels.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
A single 20% corruption condition is reported, but the study does not test a sweep from no corruption to complete corruption or report whether test error rises steadily.
Whether regularization, dropout, or data augmentation prevent fitting random labels, or whether their removal harms generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: convolutional network (left network in Figure 1; name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with cross-entropy loss on CIFAR-10 with 20% corrupted labels.
rows.value: Train accuracy close to 100%; test accuracy 55.2%.
rows.note: The caption says training accuracy is close to 100% for all three networks; the left network is the one trained with 20% corrupted labels. No chance-level comparison or corruption sweep is reported.
rows.check: Near-100% training accuracy at 20% corruption observes the fitting component of V4. The missing corruption sweep is untested coverage, not evidence of a partial effect. The 55.2% test accuracy is correctly reported.

relationships.condition: The Figure 1 CIFAR-10 convolutional network with 20% corrupted labels
relationships.reason: R1 reports near-100% training accuracy and 55.2% test accuracy, supporting fitting noisy training labels while retaining predictive signal at this corruption level.
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy was near 100%, while test accuracy was 55.2%.
